title: Classify shortest words for the braid endpoint 3214 (no κ)
body:
## Result and claim type

Answers the first open question of unpaidmoon's #6642: which shortest paid words realize the plane braid endpoint [w], w=sts=tst=3214, in the alphabet D_r(N)=I+([r]-I)N, r ∈ {s,t,u}, N rank-one on K^2.

- **Scoped proof, every field.** Sixteen explicit families of six-factor words equal [w]: four with three free projectors (e.g. `s(P) s(P') t(X) t(X') s(Y) s(Y')`, `s(P) t(X) t(X') s(Y) s(Y') t(P')`) and twelve with two (e.g. `s(P) t(X) s(X) t(X') s(X') t(P')`), X'=I-X. The proof uses only a line lemma for factors sharing one splitting and conjugation by a pure permutation; `verify.py` replays the rewrite on the symbolic words. Over F_q the families contain 4n^3+12n^2 distinct words, n=q(q+1).
- **Corollary, every field.** Every tight two-factor suffix allowed by the #6642 peel table extends to a shortest word. The concern in #6642 that a free second peel may fail to extend does not arise.
- **Finite certificate, F2 and F3.** These families are every six-factor word equal to [w]: 1296 over F2, 8640 over F3. Two engines agree: a tight-peel search and an unpruned meet-in-the-middle join, both testing exact operator equality on A⊗U.

Not claimed: completeness over other fields, any caller invoice, a κ change. Selected value 781451/250000000 unchanged; all five framework assumptions remain.

## Evidence and reproduction

CPython 3.12.x, standard library only, from the repository root:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/braid-3214-shortest-words
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/braid-3214-shortest-words/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/braid-3214-shortest-words --check-source-history
```

Local results: `PASS_BRAID_3214_SHORTEST_WORDS` (about 13 s), `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for c3398c5e2157ca3efeebc4eb88e9588745244b1b.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Completeness is proved only over F2 and F3; larger primes are an opt-in verifier argument, not run to completion and not claimed.
- Inherited and not replayed: spectator elimination (JoyboyBrian #4765), the six-factor bound and peel table (#6642), the ordered-pair defect (#6449), the st classification (#6550).
- Scalar conjugation is algebraic, not a physical basis change. No Lean, Docker or selected replay was run.

## Open next questions

- Are the sixteen families complete over every field? First step: derive the tight third-peel table symbolically after each #6642 second-peel branch.
- Do other length-three rank-two endpoints share the same building blocks (complement pairs, single-splitting blocks, conjugation)? First step: change the target constant and rerun over F2 and F3.
- What does a two-splitting realization cost physically against a three-splitting one? Blocked on a caller tariff.

## Related open work

- #6642 (unpaidmoon): source of the question and the peel table; this package extends it to whole words and agrees with its length 6 and its exclusion of u-factors.
- #6550 (ToikY): shortest words for the different endpoint st; method analogue, no shared number.
- #6449 (Nick Petalas): ordered-pair defect used by the search; not re-checked.
- No other open PR by this author created since the claim studies this endpoint or its word count.

## Task

Card `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed as in #6642 (recorded in TASK.json). Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19376725
